subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `reason: "target-none"` as a machine-readable heartbeat skip reason and add a human-facing disabled-delivery hint, or rename the reason itself?
rationale: The code change is small, but the issue sits on an exposed diagnostic contract: one option preserves parser compatibility with an additive field, while the other changes the existing reason string.

options.title: Add an additive hint
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint, and render it in heartbeat status/CLI output.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled` and accept the compatibility risk for consumers parsing the old string.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep the raw diagnostic unchanged and accept the ongoing operator confusion as low priority.

recommendation.title: Add an additive hint
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint, and render it in heartbeat status/CLI output.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the default-`none` heartbeat behavior and related system/status surfaces, making them the strongest available owner for the diagnostic-contract choice.
